info.title: MobileValidate API
info.summary: One explainable verdict per phone number or e-mail address, before you send.
info.description:
Check phone numbers and e-mail addresses in real time (`POST /v1/lookup`, up to 100 per request) or in bulk
(`POST /v1/jobs`, up to 50,000 per job): messaging-app and online-account registration, carrier and line type, spam
reputation, and e-mail account existence. `GET /v1/services` lists every check and its price.

**Try it without signing up.** Every example in this document uses the public sandbox key
`mv_test_publicSandboxn9ZgneuhR1B9CRfKG3fulym` and the documented test values (for example `+447700900001` and
`registered@test.mobilevalidate.com`, full list at https://mobilevalidate.com/docs/test-values). The sandbox key
answers only those values (anything else gets `403 sandbox_magic_only`), is limited per IP address (30 requests per
minute, 1,000 per day), accepts jobs of up to 10 rows and no webhooks. Get a personal test key for any number in
test mode at https://mobilevalidate.com/get-test-key.

**Conventions.** Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and JSON bodies. Money is a decimal string in USD. Phone numbers
and e-mail addresses never go in URLs or headers. `registered` is `false` only for a conclusive negative; `null`
means unknown. Inconclusive answers (`unknown`, `unsupported_country`, invalid, duplicate) are never charged.
Errors share one shape (`error.code`, `message`, `param`, optional `suggestion`, `doc_url`, `request_id`); branch
on `code`. POST requests accept an `Idempotency-Key` header for safe retries. Test keys (`mv_test_…`) never reach a
data source and are never billed.

**Versioning.** v1 changes are additive only. A deprecated endpoint keeps working for at least 12 months and its
responses carry `Deprecation`, `Sunset` and `Link: <https://mobilevalidate.com/changelog>; rel="deprecation"`
headers (policy: https://mobilevalidate.com/docs/versioning). Nothing is deprecated today.

Platform names are used descriptively only; MobileValidate is not affiliated with or endorsed by any platform.

post.summary: Check up to 100 numbers and e-mail addresses
post.description: Runs every requested check (see GET /v1/services) for every identifier of the check's input type: phone checks for `numbers`, e-mail checks for `emails`. Result rows come back in order: numbers first, then e-mails. The call waits up to `wait` seconds (default 10) for all answers; if some are still running it answers `202` with `status: pending` and a `next.poll_url` (or use a webhook). Checks without real-time support are refused with 403 service_disabled (param `checks[i]`) — send them in a bulk job. E-mail checks answer only whether an account or mailbox exists — never names, photos or profiles.

pending.summary: A check that is still running (answers 202)

202.description: Some checks are still running; poll `next.poll_url` (the Location header) or wait for lookup.completed.

get.description: Returns a lookup created by POST /v1/lookup, optionally waiting up to `wait` seconds for pending checks. `input` is masked on later reads; `e164` and `email` are returned. Lookups expire after the account's retention period (404 not_found afterwards).

post.summary: Estimate a bulk job for free
post.description: Validates and counts a list without storing it, calling a data source or charging: valid, invalid and duplicate rows, cached answers, the maximum possible cost (`max_cost`) and its `breakdown` per check and unit price. Checks in parts too small for the bulk price (WhatsApp: fewer than 132 numbers from one country in the job) are priced at the real-time price and listed with `reason: small_batch`. Bulk-only checks bill each country of the job at least `minimum_checks` × the bulk price when it returns an answer; countries with fewer numbers are listed with `reason: country_minimum` and their minimum is included in `max_cost`. Same body as POST /v1/jobs.

list.summary: Two test numbers and one invalid entry

estimate.summary: Test key (never charged; unit prices shown)

mixed_countries.summary: Live key, 1,000 GB numbers + 20 DE numbers (the DE part is below the bulk minimum)

post.description: Checks up to 50,000 numbers and e-mail addresses (JSON body, or a CSV upload as multipart/form-data). The maximum possible cost is reserved up front (bulk prices; real-time prices for parts too small for the bulk price, see POST /v1/jobs/estimate); cached, inconclusive, invalid and duplicate rows are released when the job finishes. Poll GET /v1/jobs/{id} (or subscribe to job.completed), then page through GET /v1/jobs/{id}/results or download the whole file. Test-key jobs complete immediately.

numbers.summary: Numbers and an e-mail address in one job

file.description: CSV. With a header row, a `phone`/`number` column feeds numbers and an `email` column feeds emails (a row with both contributes to both). Without a recognised header the first column is used and cells containing "@" are treated as e-mail addresses. ≤ 50,000 identifiers in total.

201.description: Job created. `estimate` shows how the list was counted.

get.description: Status, progress and cost of a job. `wait` (0–30 s) holds the request until the job reaches a final status (completed, failed or cancelled) or the time runs out. Keys with `jobs:read` see their own jobs; `jobs:read_all` sees every job of the account.

delete.summary: Cancel a running job or delete a finished job's results
delete.description: Running job → cancelled: rows not yet sent to a data source are released and never charged; rows already sent finish and are billed as usual. Finished job → its per-row results are deleted now instead of at the end of the retention period (`purged_at` is set).

200.description: The job after cancelling or deleting results.

get.description: One item per row (number or e-mail address) in input order, with every check of the row. Filter by `registered` / `status` of one `service`; page with `limit` and `after` = the previous page's `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: registered
parameters.description: Only rows whose answer for `service` is true / false / null.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only rows whose `service` check has this status.

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Service (code or alias) the registered/status filters apply to; default = the job's first check. With a filter, only rows of that service's input type are returned.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows (numbers and e-mails) per page. A row's checks are never split across pages.

get.summary: Download a job's results as CSV or NDJSON
get.description: Streams the whole result file, one line per row (numbers, then e-mails) in input order. CSV columns: row_no, input_masked, e164, country, number_status, service, status, registered, business, checked_at, cached, billed (for the row's primary check = first requested check of its kind), then kind, email, email_status, then per service `<service>.status`, `<service>.registered`, `<service>.<attribute>`, `<service>.billed` (empty for rows of the other kind). NDJSON lines have the same shape as result items.
Balance, reserved amount and today's usage (UTC) of the key's account. Needs `account:read`.
Request rate, request sizes, the daily identifiers cap and the key's daily spend cap. Daily counters reset at 00:00 UTC.

get.summary: Get usage by day or by check
get.description: Checks, conclusive answers, cached answers, billed units and cost for an inclusive UTC date range (at most 366 days), for the key's mode (live or test). Rows past the retention period are no longer counted.

parameters.name: group_by
parameters.description: One row per day or per check.

get.description: Every endpoint of the account that is not deleted and has the same mode as the key (test keys list test endpoints, live keys live endpoints). Needs `webhooks:manage`.

post.description: Registers a public HTTPS URL (at most 20 per account). The response contains the signing `secret` — shown only once. The endpoint stays `pending_verification` until it answers our signed `webhook.verification` event with a 2xx status. Not available with the public sandbox key.

201.description: Endpoint created; `secret` is shown only this once.

secret.description: Signing secret: the base64 part after whsec_ is the HMAC key.

patch.description: Changes the URL and/or the subscribed events. A new URL must be verified again (`pending_verification`).

delete.description: Nothing is delivered to a deleted endpoint.

post.description: Queues a signed `webhook.test` event to the endpoint (delivered even before verification). Use it to check your signature code.

get.description: Without a key: the public catalog. With a key: every check the key's account may use, at the account's prices. Lists active phone and e-mail checks; switched-off checks are not listed.

200.description: Service catalog with prices by mode.

data.name: WhatsApp registration
data.description: Whether the phone number has a WhatsApp account.
data.unit: per number and check; non-conclusive results are free

post.description: Issues a personal test key (`mv_test_…`) for a work e-mail address, protected by a Cloudflare Turnstile token from the form at https://mobilevalidate.com/get-test-key. The key works in test mode with any number (never billed, never reaches a data source), including bulk jobs and test-mode webhooks. It is shown **once** and never returned again. Each address can receive at most 3 test keys in 30 days; after that the answer is 409 test_key_exists. At most 3 requests per network per day, whatever their result (IPv6 networks count per /64). The request also asks for live access, which we review by hand. No authentication.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the company.

accept_terms.description: The company accepts the Terms of Service, the Acceptable Use Policy and the Data Processing Agreement (https://mobilevalidate.com/legal/terms, /legal/acceptable-use, /legal/dpa) and is responsible for the lawful use of the service and its results. Recorded with the document versions.

turnstile_token.description: Token from the Turnstile widget on mobilevalidate.com.

session_id.description: Optional. Set by the form on mobilevalidate.com to link the key to the page visit that led to it (first-party, per browser tab, no cookie; not sent when the browser signals Do-Not-Track or Global Privacy Control). Unknown or malformed values are ignored.

key_prefix.description: First characters of the key, for display.

409.description: No more test keys can be issued for this e-mail address right now (at most 3 in 30 days). Keys already issued are never shown again.

error.message: No more test keys can be issued for this e-mail address right now. Keys are shown only once.
error.suggestion: Use a key you received earlier, or request access at https://mobilevalidate.com/request-access.

get.summary: Check that the API is up
get.description: No authentication. 200 when the API can reach its database, 503 otherwise.

503.description: The API cannot reach its database; retry after Retry-After.

post.description: Sent to the endpoint named in the lookup's `webhook_endpoint_id` when a lookup that answered `pending` has finished. `data.summary.total` counts rows; `registered`, `not_registered` and `unknown` count checks. Test keys send the same shape with `livemode: false`. Fetch the rows with GET /v1/lookups/{id}. Every delivery carries the headers `webhook-id` (event id, same across retries), `webhook-timestamp` (Unix seconds) and `webhook-signature` (`v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256 of "{id}.{timestamp}.{raw body}">`, key = base64-decoded part of the secret after `whsec_`). Answer 2xx within 10 seconds; failed deliveries are retried for 24 hours.

Sent when a job reaches `completed`. `progress.total` counts rows (numbers and e-mails); `checks_total`, `done`, `conclusive` and `non_billable` count checks (row × check), so `done` equals `checks_total` when the job is finished. Fetch the rows from `results_url` with your key. Payloads never contain phone numbers or e-mail addresses. Same headers and retries as lookup.completed.

post.summary: A bulk job failed (subscribable; delivery rolling out)
post.description: Sent when a job ends in `failed`. Reserved amounts for unchecked rows are released. Same headers and retries as lookup.completed.

post.summary: Progress of a running job (opt-in; delivery rolling out)
post.description: At most once a minute while a job runs. Counters as in job.completed. Same headers and retries as lookup.completed.

post.summary: The balance fell below the low-balance threshold (delivery rolling out)
post.description: Illustrative payload; the `data` fields may still change until delivery starts. Same headers and retries as lookup.completed.

post.summary: A daily identifiers cap or spend cap was reached (delivery rolling out)
post.description: Illustrative payload; the `data` fields may still change until delivery starts. Same headers and retries as lookup.completed.

post.summary: Ownership challenge for a new or changed endpoint
post.description: Answer with any 2xx to activate the endpoint. Always sent, whatever the subscribed events.
Delivered even before the endpoint is verified. Same headers as lookup.completed.

bearerAuth.description:
`Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys start with `mv_live_` (billed), `mv_test_` (test mode: documented sample
answers, never billed) or `mv_agent_` (AI agents, with a daily spend cap). Keep the key in the
`MOBILEVALIDATE_API_KEY` environment variable.

Public sandbox key (safe to publish; test values only, limited per IP address):
`mv_test_publicSandboxn9ZgneuhR1B9CRfKG3fulym`

X-Request-Id.description: Id of this request; quote it to support. Also in `error.request_id`.

RateLimit.description: Remaining requests and seconds until the window resets, e.g. `"default";r=19;t=1`.

Deprecation.description: Only on deprecated endpoints (RFC 9745): when the deprecation took effect, as @<Unix seconds>, e.g. `@1790812800`.

Sunset.description: Only on deprecated endpoints (RFC 8594): the HTTP date after which the endpoint may stop working.

Wait.name: wait
Wait.description: Seconds (0–30) to wait for pending checks before answering.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Any unique string (1–255 printable ASCII) for safe retries: a retry with the same key and body within 24 hours returns the stored response (header Idempotent-Replayed: true) instead of running the request again.

Error.description: Error. Branch on `error.code`; `suggestion` (optional) says how to fix the request.

sandbox_magic_only.summary: The public sandbox key only accepts test values

error.message: The public sandbox key only accepts the documented test numbers and e-mail addresses.
error.suggestion: Use a test value such as +447700900001 or registered@test.mobilevalidate.com (https://mobilevalidate.com/docs/test-values), or get your own test key at https://mobilevalidate.com/get-test-key.
Send your API key as Authorization: Bearer mv_test_… (test) or mv_live_… (live). No key yet? The public sandbox key is on https://mobilevalidate.com/docs/test-values.

error.message: Unknown check. See GET /v1/services for valid codes.
error.suggestion: Did you mean 'whatsapp'? GET /v1/services lists every check code.

livemode.description: Mode of the key that created the endpoint. Test keys see and manage only test endpoints, live keys only live endpoints; test-mode events are delivered only to test endpoints and live events only to live endpoints.

WebhookEventPayload.description: Every webhook body has this envelope. `id` is the event id (also the webhook-id header); use it to deduplicate retries.

data.description: The object the event is about (never phone numbers or e-mail addresses).

LookupWebhookEvent.description: Envelope of lookup.completed events (same shape for live and test keys).

registered.description: Conclusive checks answering yes / data found.

unknown.description: Checks that ended unknown, failed or unsupported_country (not billed).

JobProgress.description: total = rows (numbers + e-mails); checks_total = Σ rows × checks of their input type; done/conclusive/non_billable count checks.

LookupRequest.description: At least one of numbers / emails; together ≤ 100 identifiers (too_many_numbers above). Identifiers × applicable checks ≤ 2,000 (400 invalid_request, param checks).

numbers.description: Phone numbers for phone checks, ideally in international format (E.164, e.g. +447700900001). National numbers need `default_country`. 20 or more consecutive numbers → 403 suspected_enumeration.

emails.description: E-mail addresses for e-mail checks. Normalized by trim + lowercase (no dot/plus rewriting); internationalised domains in punycode. ≥ 20 addresses on one domain whose local parts differ only by digits and/or separators (any run of non-letters is one class; googlemail.com = gmail.com), or (live keys) ≥ 50 such addresses of one pattern per account per UTC day → 403 suspected_enumeration.

default_country.description: ISO country for numbers without a country code.

max_age.description: Accept a cached answer up to this many seconds old (capped per check); 0 forces a fresh, billed check.

wait.description: Seconds to wait for all answers before returning 202 pending.

max_cost.description: Refuse the request (402 cost_limit_exceeded) if its maximum cost is higher.

webhook_endpoint_id.description: Endpoint to notify with lookup.completed if the lookup answers pending.

metadata.description: Your own key/value pairs, echoed back.

JobInput.description: numbers and/or emails, together ≤ 50,000 (10 with the public sandbox key). Identifiers × applicable checks ≤ 100,000 per job (400 invalid_request, param checks); checked before anything is stored or reserved.

Checks.description: Service codes or aliases (e.g. whatsapp, telegram, viber, carrier, spam; e-mail: email, gmail, outlook, yahoo; full list: GET /v1/services). Order is kept; duplicates are ignored; whatsapp.registered + whatsapp.business collapse to whatsapp.business. Phone checks apply to numbers, e-mail checks (input_type email) to emails: sending e-mails without an e-mail check (or numbers without a phone check) → 400 invalid_request, param checks; a check whose input type has no identifiers → 400 invalid_request, param checks[i]. At most 20 checks (400 invalid_request, param checks).

CheckResult.description: One check's answer for one number or e-mail address.

registered.description: Yes/no checks: true/false when conclusive. Attribute checks: true when data was found (conclusive), else null. Null for every non-conclusive answer.

attributes.description: Whitelisted check attributes (see Service.attributes); null when none or not conclusive. Values are strings, booleans or integers (Service.attributes[].type integer, e.g. number.spam risk_score).

reason.description: Why the answer is not conclusive, e.g. UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT, UNSUPPORTED_COUNTRY, NO_DATA.

Summary.description: Top-level counts are per row (numbers and e-mails) for the row's primary check = the first requested check of the row's input type; invalid counts invalid numbers and invalid e-mails.

examples.name: Spam reputation
examples.description: Whether the number appears in spam and nuisance-call reports.
examples.unit: per number and check; non-conclusive results are free

realtime.description: Usable on POST /v1/lookup; otherwise bulk jobs only.

unsupported_countries.description: Countries this check does not cover, per mode (ISO alpha-2, in addition to sanctioned countries). Numbers from them answer `unsupported_country` and are free; bulk jobs mark them before the job runs (estimate `unsupported_checks`). Example: iMessage does not cover mainland China (CN) numbers.

WhatsAppResult.description: Kept from the first API version; mirrors checks["whatsapp.business"] if requested, else checks["whatsapp.registered"].

ResultItem.description: One row. Phone rows (kind "phone"; older responses may omit kind) carry e164, country and number_status. E-mail rows (kind "email") carry email (normalized address, null if invalid) and email_status; their e164 and country are null.

input.description: As sent in the originating request; masked on later reads.

email.description: E-mail rows only; normalized address (null when invalid).

checks.description: One CheckResult per requested check of the row's input type, keyed by service code (absent for invalid/duplicate/suppressed rows).

suggestion.description: How to fix an invalid or likely mistyped identifier, e.g. "Missing country code: send the number in international format (E.164) …" or "Did you mean gmail.com?". Never repeats the input.

checks_total.description: Σ rows × checks of the row's input type

cached.description: Checks (row × check) with a fresh answer in your account's cache now; free if still fresh when the job runs.

billable_max.description: Checks (row × check) that may be billed, worst case (includes `cached`).

max_cost.description: Worst-case cost; equals the reservation made by POST /v1/jobs, so it can be passed as that request's max_cost.

breakdown.description: Price lines per check: one `batch` line, plus a `realtime` line (reason `small_batch`) for checks in parts too small for the bulk price, or a `country_minimum` line for countries of a bulk-only check below its minimum per country. Σ max_cost of the lines = max_cost.

unsupported_checks.description: Checks that will not run for some countries of the list because the check does not cover them (see `unsupported_countries` in GET /v1/services). They are stored as `unsupported_country`, never reserved or billed, and are not part of `billable_max`. Empty when every check covers every country of the list.

price_mode.description: Which of the check's prices applies to these checks.

reason.description: Why a bulk-job line is priced differently. `small_batch`: the numbers of these countries form a part smaller than the bulk minimum (`batch_minimum` numbers per country for this check in one job), so they are checked the real-time way at the real-time price. Send at least `batch_minimum` numbers per country to get the bulk price. `country_minimum`: a bulk-only check (no real-time price); each country group (numbers of one country for this check in one job) is billed max(conclusive answers × unit_price, `minimum_charge`) when it returns at least one conclusive answer, and nothing otherwise. The line lists the countries with fewer than `minimum_checks` numbers; countries with more stay on the `batch` line (same rule, which only matters when fewer than `minimum_checks` of their numbers answer). New values may be added.

checks.description: Checks (row × check) at this unit price; valid rows only.

unit_price.description: Price per conclusive check (your account's price). Shown for test keys too.

max_cost.description: checks × unit_price; for country_minimum lines minimum_charge × countries (0 for test keys).

countries.description: small_batch / country_minimum lines: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 countries of the line.

batch_minimum.description: small_batch lines: numbers per country (for this check, in one job) needed for the bulk price.

country_checks.description: country_minimum lines: numbers per country (for this check, in this job).

minimum_checks.description: country_minimum lines: checks billed at least per country that returns an answer (e.g. 500).

minimum_charge.description: country_minimum lines: minimum charge per country = minimum_checks × unit_price.

note.description: country_minimum lines: plain-English explanation of the line.

breakdown.description: Unit prices fixed when the job was created (same lines as the estimate's breakdown). Only conclusive checks are charged.

purged_at.description: Set when the results were deleted with DELETE /v1/jobs/{id}.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code (full list with fixes at https://mobilevalidate.com/errors.json).

param.description: The request field at fault, e.g. numbers[1], checks[0], email.

suggestion.description: Optional plain-English hint on how to fix the request.

tags.name: lookup
tags.description: Real-time checks for up to 100 numbers and e-mail addresses per request.

tags.name: jobs
tags.description: Bulk checks for up to 50,000 numbers and e-mail addresses per job, with paginated results and downloads.

tags.name: account
tags.description: Balance, limits and usage of the key's account.

tags.name: webhooks

tags.name: catalog
tags.description:
Service catalog (GET /v1/services is authoritative at run time).

**Spam reputation (`number.spam`, alias `spam`).** Whether a phone number appears in spam and nuisance-call
reports: telecom-regulator actions, government nuisance-call complaint data and community spam-report sites, plus
whether the number looks unassigned — recently offered as an unassigned number, or in a range the national
numbering plan has not assigned (a possible spoofed caller ID or fake lead) — and whether it is a premium-rate
number. It is report-based: `no_reports` means we hold no reports for the number — it is **not** a statement that
the number is safe. Countries: all, except sanctioned countries (see below). Attributes: `risk_level`
(`high | medium | low | no_reports`), `risk_score` (integer 0–100, higher = more reports or risk signals), booleans
`reason_regulator`, `reason_government`, `reason_community`, `reason_unassigned`, hint `voip_range` (VoIP carrier
range or VoIP number type; adds no points), `top_category` (most frequent report category; `telemarketing` = in a
range designated for telemarketing calls), `first_seen` / `last_seen` (YYYY-MM, when the number first/last appeared
in our data), `sources` (integer, independent signal classes), `premium_rate` (premium-rate or international
shared-cost number — a toll-fraud risk for OTP/verification traffic; adds 20 points but is not a signal class),
hint `personal_number` (personal/call-forwarding or pager number type; adds no points). Attributes may be added
over time; ignore unknown keys and enum values. Levels: `high` needs a regulator action or at least two
independent signal classes. Billing: every `risk_level` including
`no_reports` is a conclusive answer and is billed; `unknown` and `unsupported_country` are free. No report texts
and no names are ever returned.

**Live network status (`number.hlr`, alias `hlr`).** Live home-network query: `status`
(`reachable | unreachable | invalid | unknown`), `ported`, `roaming` (yes/no only, no location), `network`,
`mcc_mnc`, `country`. `reachable`, `unreachable` and `invalid` are conclusive and billed; `unknown` is free.

**Number portability (`number.mnp`, alias `mnp`).** Whether a mobile number was ported to another network:
`porting` (`ported | not_ported | unknown`), `mcc_mnc` and `country` of the current network. `ported` and
`not_ported` are billed; `unknown` (including invalid numbers) is free.

**Sanctioned countries.** Numbers from Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Russia, Belarus, Venezuela and sanctioned regions are never checked:
every check answers `unsupported_country` and is free.
